answer.answer:
Adopting a robotic process means changing the delivery and business model itself, not just buying a machine: robotic assembly is recorded as depending on the delivery model, business model and work culture, and it is one of only two things in the record made contingent on that. Alongside it, the contract has to pull the producing party into early design, the product has to be pre-standardised into prefabricated and unified components, and the workforce has to be trained, with collaborative work also tied to compliance with robot safety standards. What comes back is fewer errors, higher productivity and a cost advantage on geometrically complex work. Watch that the deployed Japanese records here sit with manufacturer firms rather than with site contractors, and none of them is tied in this material to the delivery-model enabler, so the organisational claim rests on the literature.

**The delivery model is a named dependency, not a correlate**

Robotic assembly (PR4) dependsOn Delivery/business model/work culture (RI12), on the grounds that robotics adoption in precast production rests on the environmental and organisational context, peer-reviewed [1] (DEP61). RI12 carries exactly 2 inbound and 0 outbound dependency edges, and is activated in 16 of the 50 coded cases [2]; the second inbound edge is DEP81, AT8 dependsOn RI12: adopting digital fabrication at industrialised scale depends on adapted business models, peer-reviewed [2]. Because that count is exact, it can be read as a total: the delivery/business model is the stated precondition for robotic assembly and for industrialised-scale digital fabrication, and for nothing else in the graph. PR4 itself carries 4 inbound and 6 outbound dependency edges, all of them listed, and is activated in 13 of the 50 coded cases. [2]

**What the delivery has to put in place for robotic assembly**

The four inbound edges to PR4 are the exact set of things it needs: a robot arm, RE2 (DEP11, peer-reviewed) [2], path planning, PR12, as a precondition (DEP23, peer-reviewed) [2], all-weather cover, CO12, which allows welding and assembly to proceed in a normal manner even in rain (DEP42, peer-reviewed) [2], and standardised prefabricated components, AT7, on which Japanese automated erection systems rely (DEP88, peer-reviewed) [2]. On its own outbound side, PR4 hasPrecondition prefabrication (PR2): automated overhead delivery and assembly requires extensive prefabrication and unification of materials (DEP55, peer-reviewed) [2]. So the product has to be redesigned into a standardised, unified kit before the delivery change pays.

**The contractual change: early involvement and tighter coupling**

Early contractor involvement (CO11) enablesCapability prefabrication (PR2): integrating manufacturing and assembly knowledge into design requires the delivering production party, manufacturer, fabricator or contractor, to be involved in the early design phase, and a project delivery method that involves participants in early design should be selected (DEP22, peer-reviewed) [2]. The same enabler also drives DfMA for offsite interior design and construction (DEP77, peer-reviewed) [2] and improves design management and increases digital fabrication adoption (DEP65, peer-reviewed) [2]. CO11 carries 0 inbound and 3 outbound edges and is activated in 14 of the 50 coded cases. [2] On organisational form, AT12 hasPrecondition CO10: technically interdependent systems require tighter organisational coupling such as a single firm, the mirroring argument (DEP35, peer-reviewed) [2], and AT12 is activated in 19 of the 50 coded cases [2].

**The work-culture change: skills and safety**

AR9 dependsOn workforce training (RI6): high sophistication of digital technologies prohibits adoption by less technologically familiar workers, so skills and training are required (DEP100, peer-reviewed) [2], and AR9 is activated in 44 of the 50 coded cases [2]. For collaborative working, CO6 dependsOn RI6, because the success of human-robot collaboration is contingent on a skilled workforce (DEP34, peer-reviewed) [2] and dependsOn compliance with robot saf [2]
